reason: The hypothesis proposes in situ precipitate formation at grain boundaries, but the cited evidence (E1, E2) explicitly states that no precipitates were found at grain boundaries in the single-phase alloy; instead, ductility loss was attributed to nanosegregation of elements without phase separation. E1 discusses using preexisting precipitates to mitigate segregation, not stress-induced precipitation. Thus, the key premise of stress-triggered nanoscale phase separation is directly contradicted by the cited evidence.
premises: Localized stress at grain boundaries can trigger in situ nanoscale phase separation or ordering in a single-phase HEA at intermediate temperatures.
This phase separation manifests as brittle, intergranular precipitates that reduce toughness.
The mechanism is distinct from the fast nanosegregation of principal elements to grain boundaries without precipitation reported in E2.
The CrMnFeCoNi HEA is initially homogeneous and single-phase with smooth grain boundaries.
